title: DV-PMI Surveillance Indices
subtitle: Eight market-integrity tests on the 670M-trade Polymarket on-chain panel. Patterns reported are statistical, not legal conclusions.

cards.name: Informed Trading (PII)
cards.description: Wallets whose accuracy cannot be explained by price-following alone. Binomial orthogonality test at p<0.01 with Holm-Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg corrections.

cards.name: Insider Timing Concentration
cards.secondary: flagged wallets enter at 48% of population time-to-resolution
cards.description: How close to market resolution flagged wallets place their trades, versus the non-flagged population. Lower ratios are consistent with pre-resolution information leakage.

cards.name: Adverse Selection
cards.description: Effective spread differential between markets with and without flagged-wallet activity. The textbook Glosten-Milgrom prediction is wider spreads; on Polymarket the pattern is the opposite, consistent with algorithmic market makers crowding into information-rich markets.

cards.name: Resolution Surprise
cards.secondary: flagged minus non-flagged excess accuracy, high-surprise markets
cards.description: Excess accuracy of flagged wallets in markets that resolved opposite to the consensus pre-resolution price. Flagged wallets are positive in every surprise tercile; the population is negative in every tercile.

cards.name: Wash Trading (Tiers 1+2)
cards.secondary: Tier 1: 0.0001% self-matched. Tier 2 strict: 50,646 pairs, $1.90B round-trip volume (upper bound; includes algorithmic market making)
cards.description: Tier 1: self-matched trades, FINRA Rule 6140 analog. Polymarket's CLOB does not permit self-matching at scale; Tier 1 is essentially zero. Tier 2: round-trip wash, wallets buying and selling the same token through different counterparties. The Tier 2 strict-threshold set is dominated by algorithmic market makers, not manipulators; Tier 3 (linked-wallet clusters) is forthcoming and required to isolate wash from inventory rotation.

cards.name: Matched / Pre-Arranged Orders
cards.secondary: wallet pairs with persistent counterparty relationships
cards.description: Wallet pairs trading the same markets within short windows, repeatedly, with offsetting positions. Tighter Daubert burden than wash trading because legitimate liquidity providers create false positives; reported as 'patterns consistent with' only.

cards.name: Marking the Close
cards.secondary: directional concentration in final pre-resolution window
cards.description: Concentration of one-sided trading in the final hours before market resolution moving the settling price. Limited by minute-grain timestamps in on-chain data; intraday precision not possible.

cards.name: Concentration / Pump Risk
cards.description: Herfindahl index of trader activity per market combined with single-wallet directional dominance and price drift. Flags markets where one trader is large enough to move the consensus price alone.

infeasible_tests.name: Spoofing
infeasible_tests.reason: Requires cancelled-order data, which is not on-chain.
infeasible_tests.finra_rule: Section 9(a) Securities Exchange Act; FINRA Rule 5210

infeasible_tests.name: Layering
infeasible_tests.reason: Requires order-book depth snapshots, which we do not collect.

infeasible_tests.name: Quote Stuffing
infeasible_tests.reason: Requires sub-second order submission rates, which the on-chain trade record does not contain.

methodology_note: All eight indices report patterns consistent with the named conduct rather than legal conclusions about any wallet's intent. No public page names a specific wallet address. Per-wallet detail is available in downloadable CSVs subject to the usage notice on the methodology page. We benchmark against the leading heuristic approach in the literature (Mitts and Ofir, 2026); the concordance is reported on the PII page.
